Concerns.Title: Under the Cloth
Concerns.Pitch: There is water. Sit first; this keeps. Two nights ago a woman came in off the pans and claimed the cloth, and she is under it. I have not asked her business, and I will not before the third day. Her pursuers told me anyway, at the pole, loudly: she killed a man called Harl at the salt-scales, and they are his kin. Three of them are camped in the dry wash south of town. The oath holds them at the pole until the third day ends, and not one hour after. My clan keeps the oath. Nobody here will argue it, and nobody here will walk out to the wash for her. Someone not of my tent may. Hear one thing plainly, because it is law: if you sit under any cloth in this town, you cannot carry a blade out to them. The cloth comes off the one who strikes. The oath is not for sale; her debt to Harl's kin is another thing, and a debt can be paid. And if her word has reached the keepers at the First Tent, they may settle what the oath cannot.
Concerns.Thanks: The third day ended at dawn. She drank, I asked what a host may ask on the third day, she answered, and she went out by the north road. Harl's kin broke camp in the wash and went south. Whatever was done out there was done outside the cloth, which is where such things belong.

Approaches.Label: Go out to the dry wash south of Wellmeet and face Harl's kin.
Approaches.Objective: Face Harl's kin at the dry wash south of Wellmeet

Confront.Site: the dry wash south of Wellmeet

Approaches.Label: Pay Harl's kin the blood-price on her behalf: 45 drams.
Approaches.OfferText: Pay Harl's kin the blood-price: 45 drams

Approaches.Label: Carry her sealed word to the oath-keepers at the First Tent.
Approaches.Objective: Carry the guest's word to the oath-keepers at the First Tent

Carry.Handover: From a host at Wellmeet. A guest under his cloth asks the keepers to hear her when the third day ends.
Carry.Reply: Then she will be heard, and so will Harl's kin, and the oath will say its piece between them. A keeper will be at Wellmeet's pole before the third day is out. You carried this without asking who she is. That is the first thing a keeper is taught, and you knew it already.

Refusal.Text: It is not mine to stand in. I am saying so to you.
Refusal.Reply: That is a clean no, and I thank you for saying it. The water is still yours.

Concerns.Title: Short Weight
Concerns.Pitch: There is water; the scales will wait. I will say it here plainly, since nobody has said it at the scales. The Concord says our salt reaches Tally a tenth light. I say their carters weigh it heavy when they get there. We may both be right, because my counterweight is cracked and the pan sits low. They carry under guest-right, so I cannot send them from the pole over a weight. I can make the weight true, or prove theirs is not. Their tare-book is kept at the Exchange in Tally.
Concerns.Thanks: True to the grain. Bring me salt any day and I will weigh it in front of you, and in front of them.

Approaches.Label: Re-true the pan scales: iron in the beam, or sand in the pan for now.
Read the carters' tare-book at the Exchange in Tally.
Approaches.Objective: Read the Concord carters' tare-book at Tally

Refusal.Text: I will not take a side in a weighing. No.
